session.question: How did the study use Affective commitment in the framework, and what results it give about workplace spirituality, responsible leadership, and pro-environmental behavior in Pakistan SMEs?
session.answer:
The study positioned affective commitment (AC) as a mediating mechanism within a unified structural equation modeling framework, testing whether workplace spirituality (WPS) and responsible leadership (RL) influence pro-environmental behavior (PEB) both directly and indirectly through AC. In this setup, AC functioned as the explanatory pathway linking the antecedents (WPS and RL) to the outcome (PEB). The analysis used survey data from 390 employees in Pakistani SMEs. (shah2023sustainingtheearth chunk 1)

The results showed significant positive relationships among workplace spirituality, responsible leadership, and pro-environmental behavior. In addition, the mediating role of affective commitment was supported, indicating that AC partially or fully transmitted the effects of WPS and RL to PEB. Thus, the findings confirm both direct effects and indirect effects through affective commitment, suggesting that higher workplace spirituality and more responsible leadership are associated with stronger pro-environmental behavior in Pakistani SMEs. (shah2023sustainingtheearth chunk 1)
